page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. It runs on the AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores clocked at 3.7 GHz with simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8.0 GB per-core density that aligns with memory-intensive server tiers. The instance includes a bundled 960 GB local NVMe SSD, engineered for direct-attached low-latency ephemeral storage requirements, while omitting dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark testing reveals strong single-core computational output, ranking in the top 25 percent in both stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. Geekbench text processing also exhibits top-quartile performance. Conversely, multi-core metrics settle into mid-range tiers, reflecting the physical two-core constraint. Throughput tests on large memory blocks and multi-threaded decompression tests sit in the lower quartile, alongside subdued performance in memory-bound benchmarks such as Redis operations and Passmark database tests. Natural language inference evaluations on 7B models reflect significant throughput constraints on this virtual CPU configuration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled direct-attached NVMe storage delivers dense high-speed disk resources without the additional cost overhead of auxiliary managed data disks. The high RAM-to-vCPU ratio affords strong resource density for operational configurations requiring memory caching alongside local fast storage. However, compute-bound parallelized jobs will encounter architectural scaling limits due to the dual physical core design.

The hardware configuration positions Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 for small-to-medium transactional databases, fast local cache stores, intermediate ETL staging, and web application servers handling moderate concurrent sessions that benefit from direct NVMe local read and write operations.
description: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs backed by 2 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes 32.0 GB of RAM and 960 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, with no integrated GPU hardware. In benchmark assessments, it demonstrates top-quartile single-core CPU throughput and strong text processing, while overall multi-core computational and memory-bandwidth scores align with mid-to-lower percentiles. The presence of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage provides qualitative cost and performance advantages by mitigating external disk throughput bottlenecks without requiring external managed storage overhead. The configuration delivers a balanced profile suited for database hosting, log indexing, caching layers, and web serving workloads requiring significant memory density paired with high-speed local disk I/O.
